reference_sql:
WITH ranked AS (  -- one row per MRR change
  SELECT subscription_id, recorded_at,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY subscription_id ORDER BY recorded_at DESC, event_id) AS rn
  FROM subscription_events
)
SELECT date_trunc('month', recorded_at) AS last_change_month, COUNT(*) AS subscriptions
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', recorded_at)
alternatives:
WITH latest AS (  -- one row per subscription
  SELECT subscription_id, MAX(recorded_at) AS recorded_at
  FROM subscription_events
  GROUP BY subscription_id
)
SELECT date_trunc('month', recorded_at) AS last_change_month, COUNT(*) AS subscriptions
FROM latest
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', recorded_at)

SELECT date_trunc('month', t.recorded_at) AS last_change_month, COUNT(*) AS subscriptions
FROM (
  -- one row per MRR change, numbered within its subscription from the latest
  SELECT subscription_id, recorded_at,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY subscription_id ORDER BY recorded_at DESC, event_id) AS rn
  FROM subscription_events
) AS t
WHERE t.rn = 1
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', t.recorded_at)

other_way.sql:
WITH latest AS (  -- one row per subscription
  SELECT subscription_id, MAX(recorded_at) AS recorded_at
  FROM subscription_events
  GROUP BY subscription_id
)
SELECT date_trunc('month', recorded_at) AS last_change_month, COUNT(*) AS subscriptions
FROM latest
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', recorded_at)
other_way.tradeoff: Only the latest time matters, so MAX(recorded_at) per subscription works with no window, but it cannot return the row's other columns.

solver.query:
WITH r AS (SELECT subscription_id, recorded_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY subscription_id ORDER BY recorded_at DESC, event_id) AS rn FROM subscription_events)
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', recorded_at) AS DATE) AS last_change_month, COUNT(*) AS subscriptions FROM r WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY 1
